summary: "Svitanok" (Dawn) is an alarm clock designed for the blind and visually impaired. Each morning, it wakes the user with a melody generated from the day’s weather forecast. Every hour corresponds to a musical note: higher temperatures result in higher-pitched notes, clouds make the chords sound darker, rain adds the sound of rainfall, wind increases the tempo, and NASA climate norm data sets the overall mood of the melody. Following the melody, a voice in Ukrainian delivers the precise forecast—allowing the user to first perceive the "shape" of their day before receiving the specific details.
details:
Project Description: Svitanok

1. What does it do or how does it work?

Svitanok is an accessible weather alarm clock designed specifically for the visually impaired. It bridges the gap between complex meteorological/space data and everyday practical needs by transforming real-time weather forecasts into an intuitive multi-sensory experience.

  • Software: The web application fetches real-time weather data and processes it through a custom Web Audio sonification engine, converting weather parameters (like temperature, wind, and precipitation) into distinct auditory cues. It also features a Three.js 3D scene integration for immersive interaction.
  • Hardware & Physical Concept: Designed as a bedside device, it incorporates a tactile Braille layout with dedicated physical modes (TIME, SONG, TALK, NORM) to ensure effortless, screen-free navigation for users with low vision or complete blindness.

2. What advantages does it have?

  • Full Accessibility: Unlike standard weather apps cluttered with complex visual graphs, Svitanok relies primarily on audio sonification and tactile interfaces.
  • Practical Daily Utility: It translates raw NASA and meteorological data into immediate, life-applicable insights (e.g., how to dress or whether it's safe to go outside) right when the user wakes up.
  • Dual Design Approach: Combines a responsive web application with a thoughtfully engineered physical hardware concept (Blender 3D models and Braille ergonomics).

3. What is the anticipated impact of the project?

Svitanok empowers visually impaired individuals with complete independence in daily planning and weather awareness. By making Earth observation and meteorological data universally accessible, the project promotes social inclusion, safety, and equal access to critical environmental information.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Programming Languages & Frameworks: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, Python.
  • Libraries & APIs: Three.js (for 3D graphics), Web Audio API (for data sonification), REST APIs for real-time weather data fetching.
  • Software & Design Tools: Blender (for 3D physical modeling of the bedside alarm concept and tactile Braille layout configuration).
  • Version Control & Collaboration: Git, GitHub, VS Code, Antigravity.

5. How creative is your project?

Svitanok takes a traditionally visual domain—meteorological data and weather forecasting—and completely reimagines it through audio sonification and tactile design. Instead of looking at a screen, users hear and feel the weather. Merging space/weather data with assistive technology for the visually impaired creates a unique, socially impactful intersection of innovation and empathy.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Accessibility & Ergonomics: Ensuring that every interaction can be understood without sight, prioritizing Braille layout standards and clear auditory feedback.
  • Data Reliability: Optimizing real-time weather fetching for speed and stability.
  • User Experience: Designing a calm, non-intrusive wake-up routine that reduces morning anxiety while delivering essential meteorological updates.
